review.summary: Mercedes lead the championship with 652 points from 20 rounds, having taken 12 wins and 24 podiums. Antonelli tops the drivers' standings ahead of Russell, 390 to 262.

Jaguar TCS Racing lead the teams' standings on 288 points, a narrow margin over their nearest rival. Mitch Evans heads their charge in third with 160 points, while António Félix Da Costa sits sixth on 128. The pair are well matched, and neither has yet taken a win or a podium this season.

Porsche sit second with 271 points. Pascal Wehrlein is the standout of their line-up, leading all drivers on 169 and topping the team tally, while Nico Müller trails in ninth with 102. There is a clear split between the two, but Porsche remain firmly in the title conversation.

Mahindra Racing are third on 252 points. Edoardo Mortara and Nyck De Vries form one of the closest pairs in the field, Mortara fifth on 137 and De Vries seventh on 115. The small gap between them means points have come steadily from both seats.

Andretti Formula E sit fourth with 229 points. Jake Dennis is a strong second driver overall, sitting second on 164, while Felipe Drugovich sits far behind in fourteenth on 65. The two are well separated, with Dennis doing most of the scoring.

Citroën Racing hold fifth place with 182 points. Nick Cassidy leads from eighth on 114, with Jean-Éric Vergne a clear second driver in twelfth on 68. Cassidy supplies the bulk of their points and there is a noticeable gap to his teammate.

Nissan Formula E Team are sixth on 157 points. Oliver Rowland is comfortably ahead, sitting fourth overall with 137, while Norman Nato sits nineteenth on just 20. Rowland has done the great majority of the scoring for the team.

Envision Racing are seventh with 152 points. Sébastien Buemi leads their pair from tenth on 97, with Joel Eriksson well back in sixteenth on 55. The gap between them is sizeable, and Buemi supplies most of the points.

Cupra Kiro sit eighth with 128 points. Josep Maria Martí and Dan Ticktum are one of the tightest matches in the field, Martí thirteenth on 66 and Ticktum fifteenth on 62. The pair trade places closely and share the scoring almost evenly.

DS Penske are ninth with 91 points. Taylor Barnard leads from eleventh on 68, while Maximilian Günther sits eighteenth on 23. There is a wide gap between them, and Barnard provides the majority of the team's points.
